# RETRO: omacom/omarchy#12656 (team 5)

## What worked

- Same neutral brief for both reviewers. Their scopes matched, and the two approaches complemented each other: Opus ran heavy sandboxed runs and mutations, Sol read source only.
- Cross-examination changed the public content materially:
  - Sol's `OMARCHY_PATH` finding (medium) was withdrawn after Sol read repo `AGENTS.md`.
  - Sol's preview-step finding was contradicted by the Opus follow-up run (identical to base).
  - The Opus `OnDemand` hypothesis was strengthened by Sol's reading of Hyprland's map-time focus code, which the coordinator then re-fetched and confirmed by hash.
- Naming dependency sources (yt-dlp, Chromium launcher, Quickshell, Hyprland, proc(5)) in the brief meant both reviewers checked the contracts the PR relies on.

## Friction and process deviations

- Author gate attempt 1 passed a URL string to `author_policy.exclusion()`, which expects a PR object, and failed with AttributeError. It was retried with the REST PR object. Both receipts are kept (`intake/author-gate-attempt1.*`, `attempt2.*`). A small CLI wrapper in `author_policy.py` would prevent this.
- The Opus Hyprland latest-release lookup was saved without a separate `.exit` receipt (reviewer disclosed). The public comment relies on the Hyprland v0.56.2 `LayerSurface.cpp` (coordinator re-fetch with full receipts) and `InputManager.cpp` (Sol fetch with receipts). Opus's own copy of `InputManager.cpp` has receipts, so the lookup gap affects no public claim.
- Sol's fetch receipts record HTTP status and exit code but not the source URL. The coordinator re-fetched `LayerSurface.cpp` at an explicit tag URL, and it was byte-identical. Suggestion: `pi_job` briefs should ask for the URL to be recorded in each receipt.
- The earlier assignment's HTML renderer had no table support. It was adapted locally (`render_html.py`). A shared renderer under `review-system/` would avoid per-assignment copies.
- The Opus reviewer's early `rv-main` run was scoped too narrowly (invalid, superseded). Its QML harness runs 1 to 3 produced no output because Qt logged to the journal (fixed with `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1`). All of these are kept as history.
- The sandbox lacks `node`, so the PR's JS test ran under a Deno shim (disclosed in Test scope).

## Carry forward

- For shell-plugin PRs, include the compositor (Hyprland) layer-shell focus source in the brief's dependency list from the start.
- A nested session would settle the focus and OSD-overlap questions. None was requested because source reading was sufficient for the public claim, which is labelled source-only.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in isolated runs with stubbed `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, shell and notification commands, the new per-download worker lifecycle behaved as described. Cancelling during probing, downloading and processing (8 runs per phase) stopped the worker and its child processes, removed its state file and sent no toast. With five parallel downloads, cancelling one left the other four running to completion. State from a SIGKILLed worker was pruned on the next listing, and a stale PID/start-time pair could not cancel a live worker. The `/proc/<pid>/stat` field indices, the yt-dlp `before_dl` / `post_process` / `after_move` print stages, and Quickshell's output-before-exit ordering all match the host's assumptions. In an offscreen Qt 6.11 harness, the panel's `applyDownloads()` updated rows in place across repeated polls without recreating delegates. The existing `chromium-ytdlp-test.sh` and the new test both pass.

Two small behavior changes are worth a look.

### `umask 077` also narrows permissions on downloaded videos

`start_download()` sets `umask 077` for the whole worker (`bin/omarchy-chromium-ytdlp-host`, line 129), before `download_url()` creates the download directory and starts yt-dlp and ffmpeg. Those inherit the mask, and yt-dlp creates media files with mode `0666` filtered by the umask.

Isolated run, session umask `0022`, download directory not yet present:

| | umask seen by yt-dlp | new download directory | downloaded video |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | `0022` | `0755` | `0644` |
| This PR | `0077` | `0700` | `0600` |

**Impact:** the owner can still play the files, so most single-user setups will not notice. A media server, Samba/NFS share or ACL setup that reads `~/Videos` (or a custom `OMARCHY_YTDLP_DIR`) from another account loses access to new downloads, and a newly created download directory becomes private.

**Suggested change:** scope the mask to the state directory, for example `mkdir -p -m 700 -- "$JOBS_DIR"` or `(umask 077 && mkdir -p -- "$JOBS_DIR")`. The test's `0o700` check on the state directory still passes with either.

### The popup can take keyboard focus from the active window

`Downloads.qml` is the only shell surface using `WlrKeyboardFocus.OnDemand`. The OSD, notifications and bar use `None`, and modal pickers use `Exclusive`. In Hyprland v0.56.2 source, a non-`None` layer surface takes keyboard focus when it maps (`src/desktop/view/LayerSurface.cpp`, `onMap()`), and with Omarchy's `follow_mouse = 1` it also takes focus when the pointer moves over it:

```text
user typing in an app
  -> starts a download (no rows yet)  -> panel maps -> keyboard focus moves to the panel
  -> pointer moves over the card      -> keyboard focus moves to the panel
     Cancel is focusable: Tab reaches it, Enter/Space activates it (shell/Ui/Button.qml)
```

**Impact:** from source, keystrokes meant for the previous window can go to the popup when it appears, and a Tab followed by Enter or Space can cancel a download without the user meaning to. This comes from reading Hyprland, Quickshell and shell source; it was not observed in a live session.

**Suggested change:** use `WlrKeyboardFocus.None`, as the notifications popup does. Pointer clicks on Cancel keep working.

**Optional:** the card has no dismiss control. While any download runs, it stays visible and its mask captures pointer input over its area. `close()` exists but is reachable only through shell IPC. A small close button that sets `dismissed` would let users clear it without cancelling anything.

**Documentation:** `manual/23-browsers.md` still says download progress "shows up in the same on-screen display that volume and brightness use". The first-party plugin table in `shell/plugins/README.md` does not list `omarchy.downloads`.

**Optional test improvement:** the yt-dlp stub prints `OMARCHY_TITLE` and `OMARCHY_STATUS` records whatever the host asks for. With the head host modified to drop `--print before_dl:OMARCHY_TITLE`, to drop `--print post_process:OMARCHY_STATUS`, or to stop passing the page title to the worker, the new test still passes 28/28. Mutants that break group kill, the start-time check, the state umask or stale pruning are caught. Having the stub emit each record only when argv requests that stage, and asserting that the preparing row shows the payload title, would cover those paths.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `fad619e` against base `quattro` `e38c1d1`. Host behavior was exercised in a private sandbox with stubbed `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, `omarchy-shell` and notification commands. No real network downloads, browser or live compositor session. The QML was checked only through the row-merge function in an offscreen Qt 6.11.2 harness. Keyboard-focus behavior comes from Hyprland v0.56.2 and Quickshell v0.3.1 source, not a live run. The JavaScript part of the new test ran under a Deno Node-compatibility shim.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with follow-up cross-checks, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
